extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization. It converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by the SMPL body model (including SMPL-H hand articulation and DMPL dynamic soft-tissue deformations) via a method called MoSh++.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Unified 15 marker-based optical mocap datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet; others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, and SSM). The novel Synchronized Scans and Markers (SSM) dataset was captured using an OptiTrack system of 24 optical cameras with 67 reflective markers placed directly on subjects' skin with minimal clothing, synchronized at 60 fps with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system consisting of 22 stereo camera pairs, 22 color cameras, and 34 speckle projectors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may be occluded by the body due to pose. When multiple markers on a specific body part are occluded simultaneously, unreliable poses can result.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw optical marker trajectories from 15 mocap datasets (ACCAD, BioMotion, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, Transitions) with markersets ranging from 37 to 91 markers, along with 4D dynamic surface scans for SSM.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: To handle missing/occluded markers, a dynamic coefficient q = 1 + (x / |M|)^2.5 is introduced to scale the pose prior weight, where x is the number of missing markers in a frame and |M| is the total number of markers, increasing the prior weight by up to a factor of 3.5 to produce plausible poses.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Due to inherent problems in mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and problems were either corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ maps sparse mocap markers into rigged 3D meshes using SMPL-H and DMPL parameters through a two-stage optimization: Stage I optimizes body shape and latent marker positions over 12 randomly selected frames using Threshold Acceptance graduated optimization; Stage II optimizes frame-by-frame body pose, hand pose, and soft-tissue coefficients with temporal smoothness and pose priors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++, SMPL, SMPL-H, DMPL, MANO, Chumpy autodifferentiation package
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is hosted at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de; the authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shapes, physical motions, and 4D body surface scans of subjects (two professional models signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data and mocap).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MoSh++ runtime is not real-time; hand articulation is only recovered when hand markers are present (defaulting to the average MANO pose otherwise); facial motion is not captured; potential errors from swapped or missing markers during heavy occlusions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Computer animation, 3D visualization, character motion synthesis, editing, and generating synthetic training data for deep learning in computer vision.
